items.text:
अथ वृध्द चाणक्यस्योत्तरार्ध्दम् ।
धनहीनो न हीनश्च धनिकः स सुनिश्चयः ।
विद्यारत्नेन हीनो यः स हीनः सर्ववस्तुषु ॥१॥
items.tr:
atha vṛdhda cāṇakyasyottarārdhdam |
dhanahīno na hīnaśca dhanikaḥ sa suniścayaḥ |
vidyāratnena hīno yaḥ sa hīnaḥ sarvavastuṣu ||1||
items.en: (Here begins the second half of the Vriddha Chanakya.) A person without money is not truly poor; he may well be rich. But one who lacks the jewel of learning is poor in every way.

items.text:
दृष्टिपुतं न्यसेत्पादं वस्त्रपूतं पिबेज्जलम् ।
शास्त्रपूतं वदेद्वाक्यं मनःपूतं समाचरेत् ॥२॥
items.tr:
dṛṣṭiputaṃ nyasetpādaṃ vastrapūtaṃ pibejjalam |
śāstrapūtaṃ vadedvākyaṃ manaḥpūtaṃ samācaret ||2||
items.en: Place your foot where your eyes have checked, drink water strained through cloth, speak words checked against the scriptures, and do what your mind has judged to be pure.

items.text:
सुखार्थी चेत्यजेद्विद्यां विद्यार्थी चेत्त्यजेत्सुखम् ।
सुखार्थीनः कुतो विद्या सुखं विद्यार्थिनः कुतः ॥३॥
items.tr:
sukhārthī cetyajedvidyāṃ vidyārthī cettyajetsukham |
sukhārthīnaḥ kuto vidyā sukhaṃ vidyārthinaḥ kutaḥ ||3||
items.en: If you want comfort, give up learning; if you want learning, give up comfort. How can one who seeks comfort gain learning, and how can a student have comfort?

items.text:
कवयः किं न पश्यन्ति कि न कुर्वन्ति योषितः ।
मद्यपाः किं न जल्पन्ति किंन खादन्ति वायसाः ॥४॥
items.tr:
kavayaḥ kiṃ na paśyanti ki na kurvanti yoṣitaḥ |
madyapāḥ kiṃ na jalpanti kiṃna khādanti vāyasāḥ ||4||
items.en: What can poets not see? What can women not do? What will drunkards not babble? What will crows not eat?

items.text:
रंक करोति राजानं राजानं रंकमेवच ।
धनिनं निर्धनं चैव निर्धनं धनिनं विधिः ॥५॥
items.tr:
raṃka karoti rājānaṃ rājānaṃ raṃkamevaca |
dhaninaṃ nirdhanaṃ caiva nirdhanaṃ dhaninaṃ vidhiḥ ||5||
items.en: Fate makes a beggar a king and a king a beggar; it makes the rich poor and the poor rich.

items.text:
लुब्धानां याचकः शत्रुमूर्खाणां बोधको रिपुः ।
जारस्त्रीणां पतिः शत्रुश्चौराणां चन्द्रमा रिपुः ॥६॥
items.tr:
lubdhānāṃ yācakaḥ śatrumūrkhāṇāṃ bodhako ripuḥ |
jārastrīṇāṃ patiḥ śatruścaurāṇāṃ candramā ripuḥ ||6||
items.en: A beggar is the enemy of the greedy, a teacher is the enemy of fools, a husband is the enemy of an unfaithful wife, and the moon is the enemy of thieves.

items.text:
येषां न विद्या न तपो न दानं
न चापि शीलं न गुणो न धर्मः ।
ते मृत्युलोके भुवि भारभूता
मनुष्यरूपेण मृगाश्चरन्ति ॥७॥
items.tr:
yeṣāṃ na vidyā na tapo na dānaṃ
na cāpi śīlaṃ na guṇo na dharmaḥ |
te mṛtyuloke bhuvi bhārabhūtā
manuṣyarūpeṇa mṛgāścaranti ||7||
items.en: Those who have no learning, no self-discipline, no generosity, no good conduct, no virtue and no righteousness are a burden on the earth; they are beasts walking about in human form.

items.text:
अन्तः सारविहीनानामुपदेशो न जायते ।
मलयाचलसंसर्गान्न वेणुश्चन्दनायते ॥८॥
items.tr:
antaḥ sāravihīnānāmupadeśo na jāyate |
malayācalasaṃsargānna veṇuścandanāyate ||8||
items.en: Advice does not take root in people who are empty inside; bamboo does not become sandalwood just by growing near the Malaya mountain.

items.text:
यस्य नास्ति स्वयं प्रज्ञा शास्त्रं तस्य करोति किम् ।
लोचनाभ्यां विहीनस्य दर्पणः किं करिष्यति ॥९॥
items.tr:
yasya nāsti svayaṃ prajñā śāstraṃ tasya karoti kim |
locanābhyāṃ vihīnasya darpaṇaḥ kiṃ kariṣyati ||9||
items.en: What can scriptures do for one who has no sense of his own? What use is a mirror to one who has no eyes?

items.text:
दुर्जनं सज्जनं कर्तुमुपायो न हि भूतले ।
अपानं शतधा धौतं न श्रेष्ठमिन्द्रियं भवेत् ॥१०॥
items.tr:
durjanaṃ sajjanaṃ kartumupāyo na hi bhūtale |
apānaṃ śatadhā dhautaṃ na śreṣṭhamindriyaṃ bhavet ||10||
items.en: There is no way on earth to make a wicked person good; even if you wash the lower end of the body a hundred times, it does not become a noble part.

items.text:
आप्तद्वेषाद्भवैन्मृत्युः परद्वेषाध्दनक्षयः ।
राजद्वेषाद्भवेन्नशो ब्रह्मद्वेषात्कुलक्षयः ॥११॥
items.tr:
āptadveṣādbhavainmṛtyuḥ paradveṣādhdanakṣayaḥ |
rājadveṣādbhavennaśo brahmadveṣātkulakṣayaḥ ||11||
items.en: Hating those close to you brings death, hating others brings loss of wealth, hating the king brings ruin, and hating the learned destroys the family.

items.text:
वरं वनं व्याघ्रगजेन्द्रसेवितं
द्रुमालयं पक्वफलाम्बुसेवनम् ।
तृणेषु शय्या शतजीर्णबल्कलं
न बन्धुमध्ये धनहीनजीवनम् ॥१२॥
items.tr:
varaṃ vanaṃ vyāghragajendrasevitaṃ
drumālayaṃ pakvaphalāmbusevanam |
tṛṇeṣu śayyā śatajīrṇabalkalaṃ
na bandhumadhye dhanahīnajīvanam ||12||
items.en: It is better to live in a forest full of tigers and elephants, in the shelter of a tree, living on ripe fruit and water, sleeping on grass and wearing torn bark, than to live poor among one's relatives.

items.text:
विप्रो वृक्षस्तस्य मूलं च सन्ध्या
वेदाः शाखा धर्मकर्माणि पत्रम् ।
तस्मात्‍ मूलं यत्नो रक्षणीयम्
छिन्ने मूले नैव शाखा न पत्रम् ॥१३॥
items.tr:
vipro vṛkṣastasya mūlaṃ ca sandhyā
vedāḥ śākhā dharmakarmāṇi patram |
tasmāt mūlaṃ yatno rakṣaṇīyam
chinne mūle naiva śākhā na patram ||13||
items.en: A Brahmin is like a tree: his daily prayers are the root, the Vedas are the branches, and his religious duties are the leaves. So guard the root with care; once the root is cut, there are no branches and no leaves.

items.text:
माता च कमला देवी पिता देवो जनार्दनः ।
बान्धवा विष्णु भक्ताश्च स्वदेशे भुवनत्रयम् ॥१४॥
items.tr:
mātā ca kamalā devī pitā devo janārdanaḥ |
bāndhavā viṣṇu bhaktāśca svadeśe bhuvanatrayam ||14||
items.en: For one whose mother is the goddess Lakshmi, whose father is Lord Vishnu, and whose relatives are devotees of Vishnu, all three worlds are home.

items.text:
एकवृक्षे समारूढा नानावर्णा बिहंगमाः ।
प्रभाते दिक्षु दशसु का तत्र परिवेदना ? ॥१५॥
items.tr:
ekavṛkṣe samārūḍhā nānāvarṇā bihaṃgamāḥ |
prabhāte dikṣu daśasu kā tatra parivedanā ? ||15||
items.en: Birds of many colours sit together on one tree, and at dawn they fly off in all ten directions; why grieve over that?

items.text:
बुद्धिर् यस्य बलं तस्य निर्बुद्धेश् च कुतो बलम् ।
वने हस्ती मदोन्मत्तः शशकेन निपातितः ॥१६॥
items.tr:
buddhir yasya balaṃ tasya nirbuddheś ca kuto balam |
vane hastī madonmattaḥ śaśakena nipātitaḥ ||16||
items.en: Whoever has intelligence has strength; how can a fool have strength? In the forest, a rabbit brought down an elephant mad with rage.

items.text:
का चिन्ता मम जीवने यदि हरिर् विश्वंभरो गीयते ।
नो चेद् अर्भकजीवनाय जननीस्तन्यं कथं निःसरेत् ॥
इत्यालोच्य मुहुर्मुहुर्यदुपते लक्ष्मीपते केवलम् ।
त्वत्पदाम्बुजसेवनेन सततं कालो मया नीयते ॥१७॥
items.tr:
kā cintā mama jīvane yadi harir viśvaṃbharo gīyate |
no ced arbhakajīvanāya jananīstanyaṃ kathaṃ niḥsaret ||
ityālocya muhurmuhuryadupate lakṣmīpate kevalam |
tvatpadāmbujasevanena satataṃ kālo mayā nīyate ||17||
items.en: Why should I worry about my life, when Hari is praised as the one who feeds the world? If not, how would milk flow from a mother's breast for her baby? Thinking this again and again, Lord of the Yadus, Lord of Lakshmi, I spend my time only in serving your lotus feet.

items.text:
गीर्वाणवाणीषु विशिष्टबुध्दि-
स्तथापि भाषान्तरलालुपोऽहम् ।
यथा सुधायाममरिषु सत्यां
स्वर्गड्गनानामधरासवे रुचिः ॥१८॥
items.tr:
gīrvāṇavāṇīṣu viśiṣṭabudhdi-
stathāpi bhāṣāntaralālupo'ham |
yathā sudhāyāmamariṣu satyāṃ
svargaḍganānāmadharāsave ruciḥ ||18||
items.en: Though I am skilled in the language of the gods, I still long for other languages, just as the gods, though they have nectar, still delight in the lips of heavenly maidens.

items.text:
अनाद्दशगुणं पिस्टं पिस्टाद्दशगुणं पयः ।
पयसोऽष्टगुणं मांसं मांसाद्दशगुणं घृतम् ॥१९॥
items.tr:
anāddaśaguṇaṃ pisṭaṃ pisṭāddaśaguṇaṃ payaḥ |
payaso'ṣṭaguṇaṃ māṃsaṃ māṃsāddaśaguṇaṃ ghṛtam ||19||
items.en: Flour is ten times more nourishing than grain, milk ten times more than flour, meat eight times more than milk, and ghee ten times more than meat.

items.text:
शाकेन रोगा वर्ध्दते पयसो वर्ध्दते तनुः ।
घृतेन वर्ध्दते वीर्यं मांसान्मासं प्रवर्ध्दते ॥२०॥
items.tr:
śākena rogā vardhdate payaso vardhdate tanuḥ |
ghṛtena vardhdate vīryaṃ māṃsānmāsaṃ pravardhdate ||20||
items.en: Vegetables increase disease, milk builds the body, ghee increases vigour, and meat increases flesh.
